steps.name: Integrated report with power and QC caveats
caveats: Overlapping hallmark membership means a block of related significant sets is one finding, not several

steps.context: Final synthesis. All inputs are generic CSV tables and gene/pathway lists produced by the upstream steps.
steps.question: Taken together, which genes and hallmark pathways can be reported as changed between atopic dermatitis lesional and control skin, and with what confidence given n=6 per arm and one shallow library?
constraints: Use the actual condition labels from metadata.csv throughout
Separate robust findings from single-analysis findings; never merge them into one list
State plainly if there are few or no significant genes or hallmark sets rather than reporting nominal p-values as if they were findings
No mechanistic, therapeutic or clinical speculation beyond the direct results
steps.description: Assemble the outputs of T1S1, T1S2, T1S3, T2S1 and T2S2 into a single report. A table of hallmark pathways with NES, adjusted p and direction from both runs, and a clear statement of which are robust
Annotated VST heatmap of top robust genes across all 12 samples with condition annotation and sample_01 marked
An explicit limitations section covering sample size, the shallow library, the filtered gene universe and the absence of external validation
No claim in the report that is not traceable to a specific upstream output

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix (counts.csv, 13 columns = gene id + 12 samples) from Salmon, with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 6 atopic dermatitis lesional skin vs 6 control skin, unpaired, single batch. The research question asks which genes and which hallmark pathways change, with an explicit instruction to handle the one shallow sample (sample_01, library size ~4x below median) carefully.

The plan runs three tracks. T1S1 does QC and the shallow-sample decision: it recomputes library sizes and detected-gene counts from the actual matrix, checks whether sample_01's low depth is confounded with condition (a 6v6 design becomes 5v6 if it is dropped), runs the sample-level outlier diagnostics that actually matter for a DESeq2 model (size factor, median-of-ratios sensitivity to low depth, PCA on VST, sample-sample correlation), and issues an explicit keep-or-drop recommendation with reasoning. It does not silently drop the sample — low depth alone is not an outlier criterion, and DESeq2's negative-binomial model with size-factor normalization is designed to accommodate unequal depth, whereas dropping the sample costs a sixth of one arm's power. T1S2 then runs the primary DESeq2 contrast (lesional vs control) on all 12 samples with apeglm LFC shrinkage, and T1S3 runs the identical contrast excluding sample_01 as a pre-registered sensitivity analysis; concordance between the two is what licenses any claim about a gene. Whether the Salmon counts carry a length/average-transcript-length correction is not recorded in the profile, so T1S2 must state that it is treating them as raw gene-level counts appropriate for a count model and check for non-integer values before rounding.

T2 is the pathway readout. It uses fgsea on the full DESeq2 shrunken-LFC-ranked gene list against the human MSigDB hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols) — GSEA rather than an over-representation test on a thresholded list, because with n=6 per arm the significant-gene set may be small and a ranked test uses the whole distribution. Gene identifiers in counts.csv must be mapped to HGNC symbols before ranking; the human UniProt ID mapping file is staged if the row IDs turn out to be Ensembl or Entrez. Hallmark coverage of the 12,000 measured genes is reported, since a 12k-gene matrix is a filtered subset and the fraction of each set actually measurable bounds what the test can detect. T2S2 repeats the hallmark GSEA on the sample_01-excluded ranking so the pathway conclusions carry the same robustness check as the gene conclusions.

T3 assembles the integrated report: the gene table, the hallmark table, the concordance between full and sensitivity runs, and a plain statement of what n=6 vs n=6 unpaired with one shallow library can and cannot support.

fgsea results table for all 50 hallmark sets written as CSV with NES, pval, padj, size, and leading-edge gene lists
Per-set coverage (members present in the 12000-gene matrix / total members) reported for every hallmark set

Significant hallmarks at padj < 0.05 named with direction (enriched in lesional vs enriched in control); if none reach significance, this is stated plainly rather than softened by reporting nominal p-values as findings
Ranking metric used is stated explicitly
constraints: Use the human (Homo sapiens) hallmark gene sets — never the mouse collection
Rank the full tested gene list; do not run over-representation on a thresholded significant-gene list as the primary test
Set the random seed for fgsea permutations and record it
Report absence of significant enrichment as a result, not as a failure to be worked around by loosening thresholds
caveats: The 12000-gene matrix is a filtered subset of the transcriptome; hallmark sets with poor coverage cannot be fairly tested and must be flagged, not silently reported
Hallmark sets overlap in membership, so significant sets are correlated findings rather than independent ones
GSEA on n=6 vs n=6 inherits the noise of the underlying statistics; NES magnitude is not a substitute for the adjusted p-value

steps.name: Hallmark GSEA robustness without sample_01
steps.question: Do the enriched hallmark pathways persist when the shallow sample_01 is excluded from the lesional vs control ranking?
steps.description: Repeat the T2S1 fgsea hallmark analysis using the ranked gene list from the 11-sample T1S3 analysis, with identical parameters, identical identifier mapping and the same random seed. Compare directly against T2S1: Spearman correlation of NES across all 50 hallmark sets, the overlap of the significant sets, and any set whose NES changes sign. Produce a paired dot plot of NES (full vs reduced) for all 50 sets with the T2S1-significant ones labelled, and write a combined hallmark table carrying both analyses side by side with a robustness label per set (significant in both / full-only / reduced-only / neither). Report the leading-edge overlap for the sets significant in both — a set that is significant in both runs but on largely disjoint leading-edge genes is less robust than the adjusted p-values alone suggest.
steps.context: The pathway-level counterpart to the T1S3 gene-level sensitivity analysis. It answers whether the hallmark conclusions rest on the low-depth sample.
acceptance_criteria: Combined 50-set hallmark table written as CSV with NES and padj from both the 12-sample and 11-sample rankings plus a per-set robustness label
Spearman correlation of NES between the two rankings reported across all 50 sets
Any hallmark set whose NES flips sign between the two runs is named explicitly
Leading-edge gene overlap reported for sets significant in both runs
constraints: Identical fgsea parameters, gene set collection, ranking metric and random seed as T2S1 — only the input ranking differs
Do not present the reduced-cohort hallmark result as the primary finding
caveats: With only 50 sets, a handful of sets changing status is within the noise of an 11-vs-12 sample difference; interpret the overall NES correlation before the individual set changes
If T2S1 found no significant hallmark sets, this comparison is descriptive only and must be reported that way

steps.name: Integrated report with power and QC caveats
steps.question: Taken together, which genes and hallmark pathways can be reported as changed between atopic dermatitis lesional and control skin, and with what confidence given n=6 per arm and one shallow library?
steps.description: Assemble the outputs of T1S1, T1S2, T1S3, T2S1 and T2S2 into a single report. Lead with the conclusion: the genes that are significant at padj < 0.05 in the 12-sample analysis AND retain significance without sample_01, and the hallmark sets significant in both runs — these are the defensible findings. Report separately, and label as provisional, the findings that appear in only one of the two runs. Include: a summary table of the top robust genes (symbol, shrunken LFC, padj in both analyses, robustness label); the significant hallmark table with NES, padj and leading-edge genes for both runs; the sample_01 QC verdict from T1S1 and its downstream consequence; and a heatmap of VST-transformed expression for the top robust genes across all 12 samples, annotated by condition and with sample_01 marked, so a reader can see whether the signal is driven by any one sample. Close with an explicit limitations paragraph stating: n=6 vs n=6 unpaired with a single batch gives limited power so absence of significance is not evidence of absence; the 12000-gene matrix is a filtered subset so pathway coverage is incomplete; there is no independent validation cohort in this analysis; and hallmark sets are overlapping so significant sets are correlated. Do not speculate about mechanism, treatment or clinical implications beyond what the differential expression and enrichment results directly support.
steps.context: Final synthesis. All inputs are generic CSV tables and gene/pathway lists produced by the upstream steps.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked table of robust differentially expressed genes (significant in both the 12-sample and 11-sample analyses) with effect sizes and both adjusted p-values
A table of hallmark pathways with NES, adjusted p and direction from both runs, and a clear statement of which are robust
Annotated VST heatmap of top robust genes across all 12 samples with condition annotation and sample_01 marked
An explicit limitations section covering sample size, the shallow library, the filtered gene universe and the absence of external validation
No claim in the report that is not traceable to a specific upstream output
constraints: Use the actual condition labels from metadata.csv throughout
Separate robust findings from single-analysis findings; never merge them into one list
State plainly if there are few or no significant genes or hallmark sets rather than reporting nominal p-values as if they were findings
No mechanistic, therapeutic or clinical speculation beyond the direct results
caveats: Overlapping hallmark membership means a block of related significant sets is one finding, not several
A gene that looks robust across both runs is still an internal result from 12 samples with no external replication
